review_comments.body:
**[Medium] Keep fallback indices distinct across the response**

If two deltas each contain one complete, indexless tool call with different IDs, `enumerate` assigns index 0 to both. LangChain merges `ToolCallChunk`s with equal non-`None` indices, so aggregating these chunks combines independent calls and concatenates their arguments (for example, `{}` and `{}` become `{}{}`). This affects whole-call deltas, not just the fragmented-argument case noted in the PR description. Use response-scoped call identity tracking in both streaming paths so distinct calls do not share a fallback index, while preserving explicit-index behavior. Add a regression test that aggregates complete calls from separate deltas and verifies that both remain intact.

Building on Copilot's finding, we suggest the simpler `index=rtc.get("index")`: missing indices stay `None`, keeping complete calls separate without response-scoped tracking. Please add a test aggregating two complete, indexless calls from separate deltas.

comments.body:
Done in 4f2bc273f01e1231a986d2dda70692f071146ca5. The fallback index is gone: a delta without an index now leaves `index` as `None`, as suggested, so complete calls are not given a shared position-based index. The test for a delta without indices now expects `None`, and a new test aggregates two deltas that each carry one complete, indexless call (different ids) and checks that both calls stay intact in `tool_call_chunks` and `tool_calls`.

One note: with the locked `langchain-core` (1.5.6) that aggregation test also passes with the previous positional index, because chunks with the same index but different ids are not merged there, so it works as a guard rather than a fail-to-pass test. Argument fragments that arrive without an index or an id are not joined into one call with this change.
